rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is sparse, so this experiment tests a multimodal setup with strong encoders (scgpt for RNA, imagenet_vit_l for images) and weighted fusion, which balances exploration of key design choices (multimodal integration) and potential performance. It clarifies whether combining advanced encoders with weighted fusion yields high accuracy, a critical factor for subsequent exploitation.

The existing evidence shows that config_006 (multimodal, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) achieves 0.542 accuracy. This experiment tests replacing the image encoder with resnet50 and aggregation with transformer, which could improve performance by exploring alternative modalities and more complex interaction patterns. It balances exploitation (maintaining scgpt RNA encoder) and exploration (changing image encoder/aggregation), addressing key design choices with potential high impact.

The existing evidence shows config_006 (scgpt RNA, imagenet_vit_l image, avgpool, weighted fusion) has the highest accuracy (0.542). This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method from weighted to concat while keeping the same RNA/image encoders and avgpool aggregation could improve performance. It clarifies the impact of fusion strategy, a critical design choice, without deviating from the current best components. This balances exploitation (using proven encoders) with exploration (testing fusion variants).

The existing evidence shows that config_006 (avgpool aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.542). This experiment tests replacing avgpool with transformer aggregation while keeping other components (scgpt RNA, imagenet_vit_l image, weighted fusion) consistent. It clarifies whether transformer aggregation could further improve performance, leveraging the strong foundation of config_006 while exploring a key design choice with potential for better accuracy.

The existing evidence shows config_006 (scgpt RNA, imagenet_vit_l image, avgpool, weighted) achieves the highest accuracy (0.542). This experiment tests changing the image encoder to resnet50, aggregation to transformer, and fusion to concat (config_021). It clarifies if these changes could improve performance, balancing exploration of image encoder alternatives and aggregation methods while maintaining the high-performing scgpt RNA encoder. This is the best use of the remaining budget to refine the top-performing configuration.

Existing evidence shows that scgpt RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l image encoder with avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion (config_006) achieve the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests using pca_n2000 RNA encoder with the same image encoder but transformer aggregation and weighted fusion to explore if changing the RNA encoder and aggregation method can improve performance while maintaining the successful image encoder and fusion strategy.

Existing evidence shows config_045 (pca_n2000 RNA, imagenet_vit_l image, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.5856). This experiment tests scvi_n200 RNA with resnet50 image encoder using transformer aggregation and weighted fusion, exploring if a different RNA encoder paired with resnet50 can match or exceed this performance. It balances exploitation of successful components (transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) with exploration of alternative RNA encoders.

The existing evidence shows that configurations using scvi_n200 RNA encoder and resnet50 image encoder (e.g., config_044) achieve high accuracy (0.713). This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method from weighted to concat in the same RNA/image encoder pair affects performance. It clarifies the optimal fusion strategy for this encoder pair, balancing exploitation of proven components with exploration of alternatives under the limited budget.

The existing evidence shows config_044 (scvi_n200 + resnet50 with transformer aggregation) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.713). This experiment tests scvi_n200 RNA encoder with imagenet_vit_l image encoder (a high-performing image encoder) and avgpool aggregation, which could clarify if the image encoder choice or aggregation method significantly impacts performance. It's the best use of the last experiment to explore a promising RNA encoder (scvi_n200) with a different image encoder.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l with avgpool aggregation achieves high accuracy (config_048: 0.706). Testing config_050 (same setup but with concat fusion) clarifies whether fusion method impacts performance. This is the final experiment, so testing a variation of the top-performing configuration is the best use of the budget.
